headline: Extends and updates federal programs that fund childhood cancer research and help young cancer survivors move into adult care.
what_it_does: The law renews federal childhood cancer programs through fiscal year 2028. It expands the collection and sharing of biospecimens, which are samples such as tissue or blood used in research. It also supports programs that help children who survived cancer move from pediatric care to primary care as adults.

who_it_affects.group: Children and young adults who have had cancer
who_it_affects.how: Federal support for programs that help them transition from pediatric care to adult primary care is extended.
They can continue to receive federal funding and access expanded biospecimen collection and sharing under the reauthorized programs.
Federally supported research and survivorship programs continue through fiscal year 2028.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 5, 2023, with the reauthorized programs running through fiscal year 2028.
